items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Output limit
items.summary: Google cites an industry-leading 1M-token output limit, up from 64K ( @GoogleAI , @TheRundownAI ). Measurement note : Vals lists 262K max output.

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Google’s claimed results
items.summary: Argon takes first place on 13 of 19 published benchmarks against GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. On DeepSWE it scores 77.9%, versus 74.2% for Opus 5.5 and 74.1% for Astra ( @TheRundownAI ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Research use
items.summary: The team says internal agent loops built on Argon helped complete the CK conjecture ( @mirrokni ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Artificial Analysis evaluation
items.summary: Argon scores 53 on the Intelligence Index, matching GPT-6 Astra (53) and edging GPT-6.1 Sol (52) ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Cost per task : At discounted pricing it costs $1.99 per task versus $3.26 for Astra; standard pricing would raise this to $3.98.

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Hallucination
items.summary: Its 15% rate on AA-Omniscience compares with 51% for Astra. The tradeoff is lower accuracy: 50% versus Astra’s 63% ( @aipulseda1ly ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Vals evaluation
items.summary: Argon is #1 on the Vals Index at 68.9%, at an average $15.68 per task ( @ValsAI , @ValsAI ). Coding : It built 30 Vibe Code Bench apps perfectly, against 25 for Opus 5 and 24 for Astra ( @ValsAI ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Terminal and security
items.summary: Terminal-Bench 4.0 rose from 19.0% to 57.6%. It scores 70% on CyberBench proof-of-concept tasks and 100% on IOI 2024–2026 ( @ValsAI ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Arena and other evals
items.summary: Argon is #1 in Text Arena at 1525 and #8 in Code Arena WebDev at 1679 ( @arena ). Agent Arena : It ranks #8 overall and #1 for steerability on a preliminary 3K sessions ( @arena ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: PostTrainBench
items.summary: It scores 45.3%, up from 21.99% for Gemini 3.1 Pro ( @karinanguyen ).

items.subsection: Gemini 4 Argon: Google Returns to the Frontier
items.title: Other critiques
items.summary: Commentators raised possible preference-data benchmaxxing and objected to some figures, including DeepSWE ( @teortaxesTex , @teortaxesTex ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and OpenAI’s DevDay Agent Stack
items.title: Independent evals
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol is the new #1 on MathArena ( @j_dekoninck ). Code Arena : It ranks #3 on WebDev at 1759, 70 points above GPT-6 Sol for the same $2/$10 pricing ( @arena ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and OpenAI’s DevDay Agent Stack
items.title: Cost per task
items.summary: Artificial Analysis measures $0.72 per task at max effort, versus $3.26 for Astra and $1.04 for GPT-6 Sol ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Source of savings : Sol uses fewer turns and has a lower cache-read price ( @ArtificialAnlys ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and OpenAI’s DevDay Agent Stack
items.title: Ultrafast inference
items.summary: OpenAI quotes up to 300 tok/s. SemiAnalysis reports it runs on NVIDIA GPUs at low batch sizes, not on Cerebras ( @kimmonismus ). Hands-on report : Generation is about 8x faster, but end-to-end agent tasks speed up only 2–4x because tool latency dominates ( @sa…

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and OpenAI’s DevDay Agent Stack
items.title: Product layer
items.summary: DevDay introduced dots (persistent agents with their own cloud computers), a Decisions API and computer use ( @latentspacepod ). Sites : ChatGPT Sites can now host MCP servers and turn them into installable plugins ( @mxstbr ).

items.subsection: GPT-6.1 Sol and OpenAI’s DevDay Agent Stack
items.title: Usage limits
items.summary: Users report one-off credits worth about $2,500. Others complain that usage limits were cut ( @kimmonismus , @kimmonismus ).

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Perplexity contextual embeddings
items.summary: pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview is open on Hugging Face ( @perplexity_ai ). Method : The model encodes the whole document once and pools chunk vectors afterward.

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Cohere Embed 5
items.summary: The family has Pro and Fast variants in a shared embedding space, so you can index with one and retrieve with the other ( @cohere ). Fast tier : Cohere says it beats other fast-tier models by at least 6 points at a third less cost than Pro.

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Ideogram 4.5
items.summary: The editing model targets artifact-free multi-turn edits, with open weights promised ( @ideogram_ai ). Edit fidelity : Over ten consecutive edits, 94–99% of untouched content stays identical ( @fal ).

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Video benchmark
items.summary: Artificial Analysis launched AA-Video-T2V v2.0, judged at 1080p with more than 68K human votes ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Leaders : Wan 3.0 is #1 at $12/min. Seedance 2.5 is #2 at $34.12/min, and MiniMax H3 is statistically tied at $4.80/min.

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Open and small models
items.summary: Ling-3.1-flash : A 500B model reported close to GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 ( @kimmonismus ). It ranks #2 among open-weight models in Mobile App Arena ( @DesignArena ).

items.subsection: Other Releases: Embeddings, Image/Video and Open Models
items.title: Solar Mini 4
items.summary: Upstage reports 35B total / 3B active parameters. It scores 24 on the Intelligence Index at $0.10/$0.40 ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Caching penalty : It still costs about 5x Luna per task, because only 48% of its repeated context hits cache versus 99% for Luna ( @Ar…

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: Context Language Models (Meta)
items.summary: CLMs treat context as an editable file rather than an append-only log, with context-management policies learned in the weights and no external harness ( @RulinShao ).

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: Adaptive reasoning compute
items.summary: TaH2 : Lookahead depth supervision teaches the model which hard tokens deserve another loop ( @ZhihuFrontier ). Gains : It reports +3.4pp accuracy at matched test-time compute and a 53% steeper scaling slope.

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: AutoBenchmark (Meta)
items.summary: The project automates benchmark creation. Human feedback at the ideation stage beats agents working alone, and difficulty transfers to held-out solvers ( @jaseweston ).

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: Prefill/decode disaggregation
items.summary: A steady-state analysis argues that disaggregation raises mean interactivity by about 1/(decode-time fraction) at equal batch size and throughput ( @ekzhang1 , @cHHillee ). Implication : It helps prefill-heavy workloads, not decode-bound low-latency serving.

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: Compilers and hardware
items.summary: DeepSeek on Huawei : DeepSeek released an open-source Ascend toolkit with TileLang optimized for Ascend 950 ( @kimmonismus ).

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: AI as compiler
items.summary: A model translates Triton directly to PTX, with a verifier checking correctness, races and deadlocks. Speedups on B200 reach 1.37x on FlashAttention ( @Azaliamirh ).

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: DFlash drafts
items.summary: New draft models for Ornith-1.5 give up to 2.54x lossless speedups ( @ornith_ ).

items.subsection: Agent Research, Inference and Systems
items.title: Agent sandboxes
items.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt Containers for agents, with p50 time-to-interactive of 648 ms (6x faster) and snapshots in beta ( @mgamache ). AutoRouter : Cloudflare’s model router showed about 30% lower spend in internal tests ( @ashleypeacock ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: Reasoning extraction
items.summary: OpenAI attributes a core part of a hidden-reasoning extraction campaign to individuals linked to Moonshot AI ( @kimmonismus ). Scale : OpenAI recorded 16,000 attempts from more than 4,000 users in two days, with related activity across more than 15,000 users.

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: External researchers
items.summary: Their attacks kept working on Astra until this week. Patches were hard to propagate across product versions and third-party hosts ( @JSchaeff3r , @jonasgeiping ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: Distillation defenses
items.summary: Defenses evaluated without later RL give a false sense of security. RL makes simple attacks effective ( @shidan_javaheri ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: Embedded evaluations
items.summary: Apollo Research published principles for outside evaluators who receive employee-like access to frontier labs ( @ApolloResearch ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: Provenance and transparency
items.summary: SynthID Bio : Watermarking for AI-generated proteins is published in Nature, with open-sourced tools ( @demishassabis ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: AI-detector evasion
items.summary: Opus 5.5 and Astra can rewrite more than 50% of a document without Pangram flagging it ( @ValsAI ).

items.subsection: Safety, Security and Eval Integrity
items.title: Agent reports
items.summary: A new preprint asks how transparent LLM-written reports on agent work actually are ( @jennyihuang ).

items.subsection: Industry and Policy
items.title: Factory vs Cognition
items.summary: Factory removed advisor Chris Degnan, alleging he was confiding in Cognition while attending its board meetings ( @matanSF ). Hire : Cognition announced Degnan as its CRO the same day ( @cognition ).

items.subsection: Industry and Policy
items.title: Political spending
items.summary: Greg Brockman dropped a promised second $25M donation to the Leading the Future super PAC ( @teddyschleifer ). Follow-up question : Alex Bores asked whether this also covers anti-regulation groups that don’t disclose donors ( @AlexBores ).

items.subsection: Industry and Policy
items.title: OpenAI finances
items.summary: NYT reports OpenAI is near $70B in annualized revenue and in talks to raise $30B at a $1.4T valuation, with its IPO pushed to next year ( @srimuppidi ).

items.summary: their new flagship model built for long-running coding, knowledge work and cybersecurity tasks. The ridiculous bit: it can output up to 1 million tokens in a single run, up from 64K before.
